t: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
h: The first feature-length cel-animated fairy tale: a poisoned apple, seven miners and songs that set the Disney template.

like.r: Disney's next storybook feature, with richer animation and a darker streak of peril for its wooden hero.
Another princess fairy tale, but painted like a medieval tapestry and with a far more imposing villain.
A fairy tale with the sweetness removed: the same lost-girl-and-wicked-power story, rendered brutal and adult.

h: A puppet who wants to be a real boy stumbles through temptation and genuinely frightening detours; gorgeous, and scarier than its songs suggest.

like.t: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
like.r: The studio's first feature, sharing the same hand-painted storybook warmth with simpler stakes.
Another early Disney coming-of-age tale with a child hero who must learn about danger and loss.
Another innocent wandering a string of bizarre, sometimes menacing episodes that teach him about the world.

h: A fawn grows up through a forest year of friendships, first love and one scene of loss that has made generations of children cry.

like.r: Another animal community facing mortality, with more menace and a full society of rabbits.
A young animal prince loses a parent and must grow up, with songs and a bigger dramatic structure.
A boy bonds with a fawn and learns about loss in a gentler, slower, human-centered story.

h: A curse, three bickering fairies and a dragon, drawn in flat, angular medieval-tapestry style set to Tchaikovsky's ballet music.

like.t: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
like.r: The earlier princess tale; softer in design, and with a more comic ensemble in place of a grand villain.
A later Disney fairy tale with a stronger heroine and a more sympathetic monster in place of a witch.
A fantasy with a dragon, a quest and a kindly fairy-tale narrator, for readers who liked the storybook adventure.

h: A man-cub is walked through the jungle by a lazy bear and a worried panther in a loose, jazzy road movie full of swinging songs.

like.r: The source stories are grimmer and more moral, with a law of the jungle that the film mostly sets aside.
A later Disney animal epic with more drama and a young hero who needs wise mentors.
Reitherman's next easygoing, song-filled romp, again casting animals as a lovable band of rogues.

h: A sea-king's daughter trades her voice for legs, and Broadway-style songs launched Disney's second golden age.

like.r: The next Disney musical, with a bookish heroine and richer, more theatrical songs.
Same directors, same lively songwriting, swapping the ocean for a desert and adding a scene-stealing sidekick.
A live-action mermaid-meets-man romance that takes the same fish-out-of-water premise in a gentle comic direction.

h: A bookish girl and a cursed prince fall in love among singing furniture; a fairy tale built like a stage musical.

like.r: The same songwriting team and Disney revival energy, with a younger and more impulsive heroine.
Another of the studio's songs-and-sidekicks romances, faster and funnier.
Another love story with an enchanted grumpy hero and a heroine under a curse, stranger and less sung.

h: A street thief, a runaway princess and a motor-mouthed genie in a comic, song-packed caper powered by Robin Williams's improvising.

like.r: The directors' earlier fairy-tale musical, with a softer tone and a sea-bound romance.
Also a wisecracking sidekick comedy with pop-culture gags, but one that mocks the fairy-tale form.
Another fast, charming adventure through exotic ruins with a rogue hero and a banter-ready love interest.

h: A cub prince flees after his father's death and returns to claim a ruined kingdom; Hamlet on the savanna, with Elton John songs.

like.r: The play behind the plot: a prince, a murdered king, a villainous uncle, but with a tragic ending.
An earlier Disney animal coming-of-age story that is just as sad about the loss of a parent.
A later Disney musical about a young heir who must leave home to find her responsibility.

h: A girl takes her father's place in the army by passing as a man; a training montage, a tiny dragon and a surprisingly serious war.

like.r: A later Disney musical built around sisters and self-acceptance rather than a prince.
Another animated martial-arts underdog story set in a stylized China, with more slapstick.
Another heroine fighting the future her family has laid out for her, in a Scottish fairy-tale setting.

h: Two royal sisters, one with uncontrollable ice powers, in a musical about fear and love that put sisterly love at the center.

like.r: Another Disney song-driven story about a young woman defining herself, set on the Pacific Ocean.
An earlier fairy-tale musical with a spirited heroine, a lighter touch and more slapstick.
The loose inspiration: a girl crossing a frozen world to save her friend from a splinter of ice.

h: A chief's daughter sails past the reef with a vain demigod to save her island; sun-drenched seas and a catchy, Pacific-flavored score.

like.r: Another Disney heroine and soundtrack, with a wintry kingdom instead of a sea.
Another warm ocean quest of a young one braving the unknown, with gentler comedy.
A far more serious tale of a young hero trying to heal a land cursed by nature's anger.

h: A rabbit cop and a con-artist fox chase a missing-persons case across a city of animals; a buddy-cop comedy with real ideas about prejudice.

like.r: Another noir-flavored mystery in a world where cartoon characters hold jobs and the city hides a conspiracy.
The same director's earlier comedy about misfit friends in a richly imagined world.
The grown-up version of the detective story: a city's secret that the investigator slowly uncovers.

h: A cowboy doll and a space-ranger action figure compete, then team up to get home; the first computer-animated feature, and still a perfect buddy movie.

like.r: Pixar's next world-behind-the-closet comedy, built around another odd-couple friendship.
A toy-box world that finds the same jokes and sentiment, much faster and meta.
The classic tale of a toy that wants to be loved, which foreshadows the series' feelings.

h: Closet-door scarers discover that a human toddler is far more dangerous and lovable than any child they were trained to fear.

like.r: Pixar's first hit shares the idea of a hidden world behind the ordinary one, with a similar odd-couple warmth.
A gentler, quieter story where children befriend a large, fuzzy creature nobody else can see.
A picture book in which monsters turn out to be companions, with the same mix of fear and affection.

h: An anxious clownfish crosses the ocean with a forgetful blue tang to find his captured son; sunny, funny and secretly about letting go.

like.r: Another ocean adventure about a young one leaving home, with songs and a bigger mythology.
A hand-drawn seaside fantasy of a fish-girl, softer and dreamier than Pixar's slapstick.
Another animal parent-and-child story where fear of losing a family member drives the plot.

h: A retired superhero family stuck in suburban routine is pulled back into action, in a retro-spy, mid-century-styled adventure with real wit.

like.r: Bird's earlier animated feature, more somber and sentimental, in a similar retro setting.
A different animated take on superheroes: more experimental in look, and just as heartfelt.
A far darker meditation on retired heroes forced out of normal life, with the same questions about identity.

h: A rat with a gourmet's nose helps a hapless kitchen boy in Paris; one of the most sensory films about cooking and what art demands.

like.r: A live-action tale of a cook rediscovering his passion, just as in love with food and quick-witted.
Another warm film about a love of French cooking changing lives.
A similarly whimsical, storybook Paris, with the same kind of tender charm.

h: A lonely trash-compacting robot falls for a sleek probe; the first half is almost wordless, and the satire of consumer life is sharp.

like.r: Another Pixar film whose wordless opening says more about love and loneliness than most dialogue.
The film WALL-E quotes and parodies, a cold, cerebral spaceship story on the same themes of technology.
Another story about a lost machine-world and its robots, with an environmental conscience.

h: A widower ties thousands of balloons to his house to keep a promise to his wife; its first ten minutes are among animation's most moving.

like.r: Another Pixar film where family memory, loss and an elder's regret drive a colorful adventure.
Another flying-house fantasy with an elderly character at the heart of the story.
A live-action road film about a widower facing the end of life, with more bitterness.

h: The feelings inside an eleven-year-old girl's head squabble over how to handle a move; smart about sadness and affecting.

like.r: The same director's next big-idea film about what makes a life, with a jazz-filled afterlife.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another film that goes inside a mind and lets memories play out, but for adults and heartbreak.
An earlier Pixar film that finds big feelings through a child's inner world and objects.

h: A Mexican boy who dreams of guitar crosses into the land of the dead, where a lavish world hides a family mystery.

like.r: Another animated Day of the Dead fantasy, more stylized and zany, with less emotional pull.
Another child who crosses into a spirit world and must find a way home through a bureaucracy of strange beings.
Another Pixar adventure that uses a vibrant world to deliver a moving story about elders and memory.

h: A jazz teacher dies on the verge of his big break and ends up mentoring an unborn soul; a gentle riddle about what makes a life worth living.

like.r: The same director's earlier trip into the abstract machinery of the mind, more childlike and brisk.
A live-action portrait of a young jazz musician's obsession that asks the same question about what music costs.
A romantic, jazz-soaked story about chasing artistic dreams and what's lost along the way.

h: A lonely boy hides a giant robot that fell from the sky in a small Maine town, under the shadow of Cold War paranoia.

like.r: A lonely child shelters a visitor from the sky, with the same pull between wonder and government suspicion.
Another film that makes a metal giant into a gentle character, with fewer words and a bigger world.
The short children's book the film was adapted from, strange and mythic.

h: A grumpy ogre rescues a princess for a corrupt lord and finds himself in a fairy-tale parody stuffed with pop-culture jokes.

like.r: Another beloved fairy-tale send-up with a sincere love story under the jokes.
A Disney caper with a wisecracking sidekick, played straight where Shrek mocks.

like.t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
like.r: A far cruder, sillier take that pokes at the legends it borrows from.

h: A scrawny Viking boy befriends the dragon he was meant to kill; the flight scenes are some of animation's most exhilarating.

like.r: Another boy-and-giant-creature friendship that confronts a fearful adult world.
Another child's coming-of-age through a fantastical world, more dreamlike.
A boy bonds with a dragon in a longer, more conventional fantasy quest.

h: Brooklyn teen Miles Morales meets other Spider-people in a comic-book collage of halftones, hip-hop and genuine heart.

like.r: An earlier animated superhero film built on family and pep rather than multiverse jokes.
A live-action comic-book mash-up with the same pop-art style and relentless inventiveness.
From the same producers: a frantic, self-aware animated hit with a sweet core.

h: An ordinary construction worker is mistaken for the chosen one in a joke-a-second brick world, with a surprisingly human twist.

like.r: The classic movie about toys and play, with more gentle humor and a more traditional plot.
Another inventive, meta animated romp from the same production circle, with a more emotional bent.
An earlier comedy that parodies the stories it is built from, with a similar knowing sarcasm.

h: A noodle-shop panda is accidentally named the Dragon Warrior; slapstick, gorgeous kung-fu set pieces and surprisingly warm underdog stuff.

like.r: Another animated martial hero's journey in a stylized China, with songs where Panda has gags.
The live-action martial-arts epic Panda is paying homage to, more lyrical and serious.
Another DreamWorks underdog who wins by understanding rather than force.

h: A sulky girl takes a job in a bathhouse for spirits to save her parents; a dream-logic fantasy of unforgettable creatures and odd tenderness.

like.r: The same director's gentler, plotless fantasy of childhood wonder, with no villains.
Another girl in a strange world who must outwit its owner, creepier and in stop-motion.
The classic child-in-a-nonsense-world story that Spirited Away echoes in a Japanese key.

h: Two sisters move to the countryside and meet a giant, sleepy forest spirit; there is no villain, just the feeling of a long summer.

like.r: Another easy-going Miyazaki story about a girl finding her way, a little more grown-up.
A seaside cousin: a small child befriends a magical creature in a picture-book world.
A cozy English pastoral with a similar love of nature and gentle creatures.

h: A cursed prince is caught between an ironworks town and the forest gods it is destroying; a violent and morally unsettled epic with no easy villain.

like.t: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
like.r: Miyazaki's earlier epic about people and a poisoned, living landscape, less brutal.
The classic Japanese period action epic, a major influence on this film's battle scenes.
Another big spectacle about industry against a sacred forest, much less ambiguous.

h: A young hatter cursed to look ninety wanders into a wizard's walking castle; a fanciful romance wrapped around a senseless war.

like.r: The novel is wittier and more tangled, with a different Howl and a funnier Sophie.
Another Miyazaki story of a young woman and magic, lighter and more episodic.
Another love story about a girl and an enchanted man in a magical house.

h: A thirteen-year-old witch leaves home for a year on her own and starts a flying delivery business; a warm, low-stakes story about self-reliance.

like.r: The director's other gentle, villain-free film, for younger viewers and with more wonder.
Another Ghibli story about a girl finding her talent and purpose, more grounded.
A thoughtful coming-of-age with magic, in a more serious setting.

t: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
h: A princess tries to bring peace between warring kingdoms and a toxic forest of giant insects in a post-collapse world.

like.r: The later film that explores the same conflict between humans and nature in more depth and violence.
Another ecological epic where a hostile landscape shapes politics and a young leader.
Another Japanese post-catastrophe story, more urban, hard-edged and violent.

h: A miner boy and a girl with a magic crystal race pirates and soldiers to a floating island; Miyazaki at his most swashbuckling.

like.r: Another breathless chase for a legendary relic, played with live-action stunts and humor.
A later Miyazaki flight-and-steampunk fantasy, more romantic and strange.
Another film with an overgrown lost robot world and a fable about technology.

h: A goldfish princess wants to become human to be with a five-year-old boy; a hand-drawn ocean of waves that seem alive.

like.r: The Andersen story in its Disney version, with a bigger villain and love-struck heroine.
A similar child's-eye, villain-free wonder in a Japanese countryside.
Another bright underwater fantasy built around a young fish's trek.

h: A fictionalized life of the engineer who designed Japan's wartime fighter planes, a bittersweet romance about beauty and complicity.

like.r: Another Japanese animated look at the war, this time through starving children, devastating where this is wistful.
Another portrait of a creator whose brilliant work is turned into a weapon.
The director's epic about the costs of industry, in fantasy form.

h: Two orphaned siblings try to survive the firebombing of Kobe; among the most devastating war films ever made, animated or not.

like.r: Another animated look at Japanese civilians in wartime, in Hiroshima, and more graphic.
Another war film that finds its power in individual victims.
A quieter Ghibli film on the same war from the engineer's side.

t: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
h: A bamboo cutter finds a tiny girl who grows into a princess he cannot keep; hand-sketched, watercolor and quietly heartbreaking.

like.r: Ghibli's other great story of a girl and the supernatural, busier and more joyful.
Another hand-drawn Celtic fairy tale of a child pulled between worlds.
The same director's earlier film: wartime realism, where this is folktale, and just as moving.

h: A biker gang boy gains terrible powers in neo-Tokyo; a motorcycle-and-mutation explosion that changed how the world saw anime.

like.r: A cooler, more philosophical cyberpunk anime on the same city-of-the-future tradition.
The neon dystopia that influenced Akira's city, live-action and slower.
Another dark 1990s anime film, more psychological and personal in scale.

h: A cyborg agent hunts a hacker and questions what is left of her self; a rainy, hushed city and a contemplative action film.

like.r: A live-action ancestor in look and theme: what makes someone human in a neon, rain-slicked city.
A direct admirer: reality, hacking and bodies, with faster action and less quiet.
A more kinetic, wilder anime view of a technological Japan.

h: A pop idol turns to acting and finds her sense of self splintering as a stalker closes in; reality slips with each scene.

like.r: A live-action descendant of the same idea: a performer's fragile identity and a descent into paranoia.
The same director's later, brighter dream-heist, equally slippery but playful.
Another fractured Hollywood nightmare of identity, in live action.

h: A therapist enters patients' dreams with a stolen device and a parade of surreal imagery bursts into the waking world.

like.r: The better-known dream-heist that borrows ideas from Kon's film, more orderly and big-budget.
The same director's earlier, much darker study of reality coming apart.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another film that treats the mind as a place you can enter, with a more romantic focus.

h: A country girl and a Tokyo boy swap bodies in their sleep and fall for each other; luminous skies, a pop score and a turn that pays off.

like.r: The director's follow-up that shares the weather-as-feeling and teen romance with a more explicit cost.
Another 2016 teen story about connection and regret, quieter and more painful.

like.t: The Girl Who Leapt Through Time
like.r: An earlier anime romance with time travel and a young heroine.

h: A former bully tries to make amends to the deaf girl he tormented in grade school; a tender study of guilt and second chances.

like.r: The other big anime hit of the same year, more fantastical and swoony.
A live-action story of a child who is different at school, more earnest and less haunted.
Another story about a damaged young person slowly accepting forgiveness.

h: A bored girl crawls through a hidden door into a better version of home, with button eyes; stop-motion with real chills.

like.r: The short novel it is based on, which is even creepier and more unsettling.
The director's earlier stop-motion fantasy, more musical and cheerfully macabre.
Another girl trapped in a seductive other world, less menacing and more wondrous.

h: Halloween Town's skeleton king stumbles into Christmas and tries to take it over; spooky, handmade and full of Danny Elfman songs.

like.r: Another macabre stop-motion musical romance in the same gothic style.
The same director's creepier, more dreadful fairy tale.
Burton's gothic suburban fable of a misfit, more romantic and live-action.

h: A boy with a magic shamisen sets out to find his father's armor in an origami-filled, hand-built world; surprisingly mournful.

like.r: Another Laika-style stop-motion fairy tale with real darkness for young viewers.
A similar Japanese-flavored spirit-world quest by an animation master.
A more epic and violent folklore adventure in the same setting.

h: Hens plot to escape a Yorkshire farm in a clay-animated parody of prison-break movies, full of British gags.

like.r: The WWII prison-break classic it lovingly parodies, serious and star-studded.
Another stop-motion animal heist comedy on a farm, drier and more stylized.
A far darker story of farm animals taking control of their lives.

h: A mute girl who is half-selkie and her older brother journey through Irish folklore to save the fairy world; hand-painted and sad.

like.r: The studio's first feature, illuminated-manuscript-flat and about monks and fairies.

like.t: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
like.r: Another hand-drawn folktale about a child between worlds, also heartbreaking.
A warmer story of siblings and nature spirits, with less sorrow.

h: A young monk helps an illuminator finish a famous book while Vikings approach; flat, jewel-bright and full of woodland spirits.

like.r: The director's follow-up that takes the same style into a more emotional, modern family story.
The third film in the same Irish folklore style, with a more thrilling plot.
Another stylized fairy tale about the power of art and story.

h: An English hunter's daughter befriends a girl who turns into a wolf in an Irish forest, in woodcut-like hand-drawn animation.

like.r: Another story of humans against a forest and its spirits, more violent and epic.
The director's earlier film, more mournful and slower in pace.
Another story about a young person who befriends the creatures her people hunt.

h: A girl grows up through Iran's revolution and war and then exile in Europe, in stark black-and-white ink with sharp humor.

like.r: The graphic memoir it is drawn from, with more detail and a steady, wry voice.
Another animated film in which a real history is told through memory and politics.
Another landmark comics memoir of a political catastrophe, told in stark black and white.

h: A reformed chicken thief takes up his old trade and sets three farmers on him, in handmade stop-motion with Anderson's deadpan symmetry.

like.r: The slim children's book it expands, sharper and meaner than the film's family comedy.
Anderson's live-action family comedy with the same deadpan wit and wounded parent.
Another British stop-motion farm caper, broader and more slapstick.

h: A filmmaker interviews old comrades to recover his lost memories of the 1982 Lebanon war, in animated, nightmarish interviews.

like.r: Another animated, personal film about Middle Eastern conflict, with more humor.
A live-action war film that also takes a hallucinatory tone and treats war as a descent.
Another animated film in which war is not heroic but overwhelmingly sad.

h: A grandmother and her dog chase kidnappers of a cyclist across the Atlantic, in near-wordless, grotesque and jazzy animation.

like.r: Another quirky French fantasy of eccentric characters and odd detail, in live action.
The director's following animated film, quieter and sadder, based on a Jacques Tati script.
Another handmade, mostly wordless comic invention where a dog is smarter than the humans.

h: A customer-service author in a Cincinnati hotel hears everyone as one voice until he meets a woman who sounds different; stop-motion for grown-ups.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another Kaufman script about love and memory, warmer and more fantastical.
Another film set in a hotel about two lonely people and a brief connection.
Another Kaufman script, more absurd and comic, about the borders of identity.

h: An unauthorized Dracula whose rat-faced count creeps through shadows; silent cinema's most enduring vampire.

like.r: The sound-era version of the same legend, more talkative and elegant, with Bela Lugosi's accent.
The novel Murnau borrowed from without permission, told in letters and diaries rather than shadows.
Another German silent nightmare, with painted sets and a twisted, expressionist look.

h: A sleepwalker murders at a carnival showman's command, in jagged painted sets that put the madness on screen.

like.r: Another landmark of German expressionism, with real locations and a fiercer monster.
Another German silent classic, a grand sci-fi vision instead of a small fever dream.
A modern thriller that also keeps asking who is mad and who is telling the story.

h: A scientist builds a man from corpses and the creature turns out to be a child in a giant's body; sympathy for the monster begins here.

like.r: The novel is far more articulate and philosophical, with an eloquent creature and a guilt-stricken maker.
A modern reinvention of a made woman, absurd and sensuous where Whale is solemn.
Burton's gothic fable of a gentle artificial man, carrying Whale's sympathy for the creature.

h: Bela Lugosi's hypnotic count moves from Transylvania to London drawing rooms; stagey and slow, but the image of the vampire was set here.

like.r: The silent predecessor, more grotesque and truly eerie, without Lugosi's suave charm.
The novel behind it, told through diaries and letters with more menace and more characters.
A lavish, romantic retelling that keeps the story and adds operatic excess.

h: A woman on the run stops at a lonely motel; Hitchcock's famous shocks rewired what a thriller could do to its audience.

like.r: The pulp novel behind it, shorter and nastier, with a more explicit look inside its killer's mind.
Released the same year with a similar killer's-eye view, colorful and far less embraced at first.
The stalk-and-slash descendant that borrows Psycho's tension and violin-like score.

h: A flirtation in a California bay town turns into a siege as ordinary birds turn on the residents, with no explanation offered.

like.r: Hitchcock's other great shocker, tighter and more human, with a murderer instead of a swarm.
Another small-town siege by an unexplained animal threat, with a stronger sense of fun.
The short story behind it, bleaker and set in wartime Cornwall.

h: A shy camera operator films the fear of the women he kills, in a lurid Technicolor London that accuses the audience of watching.

like.r: The same year's far more successful killer study, in black-and-white and without the camera theme.
Another film about voyeurism and the pleasures and dangers of looking, more playful.
A thriller about recording, watching and obsession in the Hitchcock tradition.

h: A surgeon abducts young women to graft a new face onto his disfigured daughter; poetic, hushed and still shocking in its operating-room scene.

like.r: Another black-and-white shocker of the same year with a disturbed family at its center.
A glossy descendant, with another obsessive surgeon remaking a captive's body.
The classic science-gone-wrong story, less dreamlike and more theatrical.

h: Four people spend a night in a huge old house, and a lonely woman begins to hear it call her; scares made of sound and suggestion.

like.r: The novel behind it, subtler and sadder, living inside Eleanor's head.
Another black-and-white ghost story in which you can't tell if it's the house or the mind.
A later hushed, fog-and-candlelight haunted-house film built on dread and implication.

h: Strangers barricade in a farmhouse as the dead rise; a low-budget siege that turns into a bleak study of panic and distrust.

like.r: An earlier black-and-white paranoid siege about a town turning into something else, with a Cold War subtext.
A later outbreak thriller that kept the grim tone and added speed.
The novel that inspired Romero: one man besieged in his home by a world of the infected.

h: A pregnant young wife slowly suspects her friendly neighbors; a paranoid Manhattan horror where nobody ever raises their voice.

like.r: The faithful novel, brisk and bookish, filled with the same slow gaslighting.
Polanski's earlier study of a woman's fear in a closed apartment, colder and more subjective.
A modern family horror about a cult and a mother's grief, louder and more extreme.

h: A withdrawn manicurist left alone in her sister's flat begins to hallucinate and slide into violence; an airless portrait of fear of men.

like.r: Polanski's next apartment-bound paranoia, bigger in scope and more focused on conspiracy.
Another study of a young woman fraying under pressure, with a more glossy surface.
Another black-and-white study of identity and breakdown, more art-house and abstract.

h: Four Lafcadio Hearn ghost stories shot on painted soundstages in lush color; a slow, dreamlike anthology of curses and spirits.

like.r: Another 1964 Japanese folk horror, black-and-white and far more raw and earthy.
A later Japanese ghost story that revived the same pale, long-haired spirit for modern viewers.
A later Japanese horror that starts as a quiet romance and ends in shocking cruelty.

h: Two women in a sea of reeds kill stray soldiers for their armor; then a demon mask enters their lives in a feverish tale of hunger and desire.

like.r: Made the same year, more polished and spectral, a quieter anthology of ghost stories.
Another folk-horror that makes a rural landscape and its customs the real threat.
Another stylized, misty feudal Japan film about ambition and fate.

h: A girl in Georgetown changes and two troubled priests are called; a serious film about doubt that is also frightening and nauseating.

like.r: The novel, more cerebral and focused on faith, from the writer of the screenplay.
A quieter, more social devil-in-the-family horror, subtler and more insidious.
Another film of satanic dread, more a thriller of conspiracy and omens than possession.

h: A couple mourn their drowned daughter in a decaying Venice where a psychic warns them; mournful, fragmented and unforgettably cut.

like.t: Don't Look Now and Other Stories
like.r: The story it is based on, sparer and equally chilling.
A modern family-in-grief horror, much louder and more graphic.
Another film about a parent's grief for a lost child that turns into a ghost story.

h: A devout policeman searches for a missing girl on a Scottish island of cheerful pagans; folk songs, maypoles and rising unease.

like.r: A modern daylight folk horror in the same spirit of cheerful, communal menace.
A darker, more austere take on rural superstition set in colonial New England.
A comic cousin with another outsider cop in a village with a sinister secret.

h: Young travelers meet a family of cannibals in rural Texas; a sweaty, grimy nightmare far less gory than its reputation but harrowing.

like.r: Another grindhouse horror of travelers hunted by a feral rural family.
A more polished suspense and the template of the later slasher, with less raw grime.
Not horror, but also city men terrorized in a hostile rural place.

h: Sorority sisters receive obscene phone calls over the holidays while someone hides in the attic; a proto-slasher with real menace.

like.r: The slasher template that came after, more polished and iconic.
A later, self-aware slasher that also builds on terrifying phone calls.
The earlier killer-in-the-house chiller whose shadow lies over all of these.

h: A police chief, an oceanographer and a grizzled fisherman hunt a great white after a summer town ignores the warnings.

like.r: The bestselling novel, soapier, with more small-town affairs and a nastier ending.
Another small coastal town besieged by an animal menace, bleaker and unexplained.
Another monster movie that withholds the creature and builds dread through craft and a tough crew.

h: A bullied, sheltered girl with telekinetic powers goes to the prom; a sad teen story that turns into a famous bloodbath.

like.r: King's first novel, told partly in news clips and reports, with a longer reach.
Another horror about a young woman and malign forces closing in, quieter and more subtle.
A dark comedy of high-school cruelty and revenge, jokes where Carrie has dread.

h: A diplomat's adopted son is the Antichrist and people around him keep dying in elaborate accidents; devil-baby dread played as a thriller.

like.r: The more serious and more harrowing satanic film of the same era.
A more intimate and ambiguous demonic-pregnancy story.
A later film in which elaborate fatal accidents are the main attraction.

h: An American dancer joins a ballet academy in Germany that hides a coven; saturated reds and blues and a screeching Goblin score.

like.r: A ballet thriller with the same mix of art and terror, more psychological than supernatural.
A pop-opera horror with the same flamboyant style, much more comic.
A modern cult horror, with far more dread of family than Argento's fairy-tale surface.

h: A masked escapee returns to his hometown to stalk teen babysitters on Halloween night; patient camerawork and a famous piano theme.

like.r: The thriller Carpenter learned from, and a source of the stalking suspense.
A knowing later slasher that plays with the rules Halloween set up.
The earlier holiday stalker film, grimmer and less polished.

h: Four survivors hole up in a shopping mall as zombies shuffle through it by habit; gory satire of consumer life.

like.r: The bleaker, black-and-white original that started the zombie film and carries real dread.
A British comedy of the same zombie apocalypse that adores this film.
A faster, more frightening infected film with the same bleak outlook.

h: The crew of a mining ship lets something aboard; a grimy haunted-house film in space with a creature designed by H. R. Giger.

like.r: Another isolated-crew monster film, with more paranoia and more messy practical effects.
Another film in which a creature picks off its group and the build-up matters more than the monster.
A later haunted-ship space horror, much gorier and less subtle.

h: Seven schoolgirls visit an aunt's country house that eats them; candy-colored, collage-like and gleefully absurd.

like.r: Another 1977 horror that is more about style and color, though far more serious.
Another horror that mixes shock and slapstick, in a cabin instead of a candy-colored mansion.
A Western haunted-house comedy full of wild invention.

h: A struggling writer takes a winter caretaker job at a vast empty hotel; long steady-cam hallways and a family coming apart.

like.r: The novel, with a more sympathetic Jack, an overtly haunted hotel and a different ending.
The earlier haunted-house classic, which relies on sound and suggestion.
A modern family horror with a similar slow squeeze and sense of fate.

h: Five friends in a cabin read from a book of the dead; low-budget, gory and wildly inventive with a swooping camera.

like.r: A grim black-and-white siege with a similar shoestring ingenuity.
Another raw, low-budget nightmare that works by relentless pressure.
A knowing later film that plays with this cabin-in-the-woods setup.

h: Researchers in Antarctica discover that an alien can imitate any of them; paranoia, snow and grotesque practical effects.

like.r: Another isolated-crew creature film, with a single monster and more elegance.
The novella it comes from, a terse pulp tale about the same shape-shifting visitor.
A black-and-white paranoia tale where no one can be trusted.

h: A suburban family's house becomes haunted and their youngest daughter is pulled into the television; Spielberg-produced scares.

like.r: A subtler haunted house that doesn't show its ghosts.
A modern haunting about a besieged family and the experts who help.
The other suburban family film of that year, benign in place of terrifying.

h: Two American backpackers are mauled on the Yorkshire moors; a comic horror with a shocking transformation scene and a ghost friend.

like.r: A werewolf film from the same year, more satirical and less funny.
Another British horror-comedy full of affectionate gore and mates.
Another film where gore turns to slapstick.

h: Teenagers are murdered in their sleep by a burned man with a glove of knives; a slasher fought in dreams.

like.r: The grounded and silent slasher, in comparison to Freddy's quips and dream logic.
Craven's later, more self-aware slasher with a human killer.
An animated film where dreams bleed into reality, in a more playful way.

h: A brilliant, reckless scientist splices his genes with a fly; a romance that turns into a slow, sad physical decay.

like.r: Another 1980s film with spectacular, tactile creature effects and a bleak mood.
The director's earlier body horror, colder and weirder.
The original story of a scientist undone by his own experiment.

h: A cable executive hunting extreme TV discovers a signal that alters his body and mind; media paranoia and fleshy hallucination.

like.r: The director's later, more emotional body horror.
Another bodily, dreadful nightmare in an industrial world.
A realistic satire of television's power over viewers.

h: A puzzle box summons leather-clad beings who offer pain as pleasure, while a woman feeds a dead lover back to life.

like.r: The novella behind it, shorter and more erotic and philosophical.
Another 1980s body horror about desire and flesh.
Another Clive Barker story brought to the screen, with more social bite.

h: A grad student studying urban legends summons a hook-handed ghost in a Chicago housing project; elegiac, bloody and about who gets believed.

like.r: Another horror that uses its monster to examine race in America, more satirical.
Also from Clive Barker's fiction, more gory and abstract.
Another film built around a supernatural killer summoned by belief and story.

h: A masked killer terrorizes a California town whose teens know every horror rule; a whodunit that is scary and a send-up of its genre.

like.r: The classic slasher that Scream talks about, serious and silent.
Craven's earlier, supernatural slasher, less comic.
Another film that takes apart horror conventions while delivering them.

h: A reporter investigates a videotape that kills viewers in seven days; slow, grey dread and one unforgettable image.

like.r: The American remake, glossier and more explicit but with the same premise.
The older cinematic Japanese ghost tradition behind it.
A later film built on a curse that spreads and cannot be escaped.

h: Three film students vanish in the Maryland woods and their footage is all that is left; terror made from sound and not seeing.

like.r: A found-footage monster film on a bigger scale and with a visible creature.
Another raw, documentary-feeling horror about young people lost in dangerous territory.
A later forest horror where the dread comes from the woods and the isolation.

h: A child psychologist treats a frightened boy who sees dead people; quiet, humane scares building to a famous reveal.

like.r: Another hushed ghost story whose final turn changes how you see it.
The director's following film, slower and more sorrowful, in the superhero genre.
Another ghost story about a child and the grief of adults.

h: A widower stages a fake audition to find a new wife; a gentle romance that curdles into one of horror's cruelest endings.

like.r: Another film where a caring woman turns out to be a captor.
Another extreme Asian film where revenge is painful and shocking.
An animated 1990s Japanese thriller of obsession, with more identity play.

h: A mother in a fog-bound island manor keeps her photosensitive children in the dark as servants and sounds unsettle her.

like.r: Another quiet ghost story built around a final twist.
The older house of suggestion and sound that inspired this kind of film.
The classic governess ghost story, which also leaves its ghosts open to doubt.

h: A bike courier wakes from a coma to an empty London and fast, rage-infected people; a grimy, shaky-cam outbreak film.

like.r: The grim founding zombie siege, slower and black-and-white.
The classic British novel in which a man wakes up to a ruined empty London.
A later fast-zombie film, set on a train and more emotional.

h: A journalist investigates a cursed tape that kills in a week; the remake that made Japanese horror a Hollywood business.

like.r: The Japanese original, more restrained and eerier.
A prestige ghost story of the same era with a child at its center.
A later curse-that-spreads film, more stylized.

h: Six women go caving in the Appalachians after a tragedy and the tunnel collapses behind them; claustrophobia before the creatures arrive.

like.r: Another film of a group trapped in the dark with something hunting them.
Another isolated group torn apart by paranoia and horror.
Another film in which city friends meet violence in a wild gorge.

h: A woman restores her childhood orphanage as a home and her young son vanishes; a ghost story that is mostly a mother's grief.

like.r: Another Spanish-language dark fantasy where a child's world holds terror.
Another Spanish-made hushed ghost story about a mother and her children.
Another ghost story rooted in parents mourning a child.

h: A bullied Swedish boy befriends a strange girl who moves in next door; a snow-quiet vampire story that is also a tender, chilling love story.

like.r: The novel is longer and bleaker, with more of the surrounding social decay.
Another film about a young vampire and her bond with a human, lush and operatic.
A non-horror friendship story among outsider boys and the first brush with death.

h: A widowed mother and her unruly son are haunted by a pop-up-book monster; a horror film about the weight of grief and exhaustion.

like.r: Another family horror shaped by grief, much more extreme.
Another ghost story about a mother's love and a missing child.
Another film in which a woman's fear about her child is both real and doubted.

h: After a sexual encounter a teenager is stalked by a relentless slow-walking entity; synth score, empty Detroit streets and constant dread.

like.r: The suburban stalker film and Carpenter-style synth score this one echoes.
Another teen horror where an unstoppable force pursues teens in their ordinary homes.
Another curse that can be passed on but not stopped.

h: A Puritan family exiled to the edge of a forest in 1630 begins to crack as something stalks them; period-accurate speech and spare dread.

like.r: Eggers's second film, also period, harsh and claustrophobic, with more madness.
The classic play on witch hysteria and Puritan fear in a nearby era.
Another folk horror of faith and the countryside, in a lighter key.

h: A workaholic father and his daughter are trapped on a high-speed train as a zombie outbreak spreads; relentless and surprisingly moving.

like.r: The film that made zombies fast and bleak, more grim and less sentimental.
Another Korean thriller on a train, about class instead of the undead.
A global account of a zombie plague, broader and more journalistic.

h: A Black photographer meets his white girlfriend's family in a leafy estate; a social thriller whose politeness hides something monstrous.

like.r: Another suburban horror of a place that is too perfect, about gender instead of race.
Another horror of a protagonist surrounded by smiling people with a plan.
An earlier horror film that tied its monster to race in America.

h: After a grandmother dies, a family of miniaturists finds itself coming apart in grief and something worse; devastating and nerve-shredding.

like.r: A classic cult-in-the-family horror, subtler and quieter.
A smaller horror of grief in a family, less extreme.
An earlier, more elegiac film in which grief for a child and the supernatural are intertwined.

h: A family lives in silence because blind creatures hunt by sound; a lean, tense thriller held together by a believable family.

like.r: Another family under alien siege on a farm, slower and about faith.
Another monster film that holds back its creature for suspense.
A bleak post-apocalyptic father-and-child survival story, with no monsters but humans.

h: A grieving woman joins her boyfriend at a Swedish midsummer festival; bright flowers, white robes and an unnerving ritual.

like.r: The folk-horror classic it follows closely, more playful and more ironic.
The director's first film, darker and set in the dark of a house.
Another saturated, stylized horror about a woman in a closed group.

h: A family on a beach vacation is attacked at home by sinister red-clad doubles; a home-invasion thriller with a puzzle about class.

like.r: Peele's first film, tighter and more focused on its satire.
A far more severe home-invasion film that also targets its audience.
A leaner home-invasion horror where masked strangers terrorize a couple, with no explanation at all.

h: Two lighthouse keepers on a rock off New England descend into drink, rivalry and delirium; shot in square black-and-white with salty speech.

like.r: Eggers's debut, also period-perfect, but more of a slow-burn family dread.
Another film about isolation turning a man mad, in a hotel in place of a lighthouse.
A sea novel of obsession, with the same weathered speech and mythic sense.

h: A woman arrives at her rental to find a stranger already inside; a trapdoor script that keeps changing what it is about.

like.r: Another modern horror that sets up one thing and delivers a sharper idea.
The classic that also upends your expectations a third of the way in.
Another film about visitors finding something terrible in a house.

h: Paranormal investigators help a family in a Rhode Island farmhouse; old-school, well-built scares with a crowd-pleasing rhythm.

like.r: An earlier family haunting with more special effects and Spielberg's touch.
The serious and grimmer possession film that these films owe much to.
The classic haunted house, where scares come from restraint.

h: A vegetarian vet student's first week of hazing awakens a hunger for meat; a coming-of-age film that is gory and darkly funny.

like.r: Another teen-girl horror about a body changing and the school that punishes it.
Another foreign horror that treats monstrous appetite as an outsider's coming-of-age.
Another body-horror film about change that is both disgusting and moving.

h: A bumbling village policeman investigates a spreading sickness and a stranger from Japan; part comedy, part possession, all dread.

like.r: Another Korean rural investigation that moves from comedy to despair.
The classic possession film that The Wailing doubles down on and complicates.
Another film about faith, fear and a family who can't tell where evil is coming from.
